answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, transferable stake before it may submit bids or vote on work. When a randomly selected audit finds fraud, the protocol slashes that identity’s stake and distributes part to the challenger; honest agents recover theirs after a delay. Splitting one operator across many identities does not multiply influence without multiplying locked capital, and each extra identity raises the amount at risk. A sable ember may drift through an ocean, but a sybil fleet must still pay that cost.
